message.content: The earliest non‑biblical mention of Jesus that scholars consider reliable comes from the Jewish historian **Flavius Josephus** in his *Antiquities of the Jews* (book 18, chapter 3), written around AD 93–94. In this passage—often called the Testimonium Flavianum—Josephus refers to Jesus as “the Christ” and describes him as a wise man who was crucified under Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius. This text predates the earliest Christian writings by several decades and is generally accepted as the first historical record of Jesus outside the New Testament.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?" They want earliest reference from historical record. We need to provide answer. According to historians, earliest references include Josephus (Antiquities 18.3) and Tacitus (Annals 15.44). Also maybe Pliny the Younger. But earliest is Josephus, around AD 93-94. So we can answer that. No function call needed.
